run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:49:03Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Alert RequestErrorRate for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is consistent with a chain I traced end to end: frontend-proxy returns HTTP 504 upstream timeouts on POST /api/checkout because the frontend's call to checkout hangs, and checkout hangs inside its Kafka publish. Evidence: a proxy access log shows "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout against upstream "frontend" with 15000-15014 ms durations logged throughout 09:44-09:56Z (261 matching lines), and trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 shows proxy ingress 504 at 15.0 s -> frontend POST /api/checkout 89.08 s -> checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.08 s -> checkout "orders publish" 88.87 s with status ERROR and otel.status_description "circuit breaker is open". checkout's own logs at 09:52:24-09:52:59Z repeat "Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open" and "Failed to write message: kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker" with repeated "client/metadata fetching metadata for [orders] from broker kafka:9092". A chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh) spawns a new NetworkChaos object every minute and each spawn reports chaos applied to pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l and both kafka pods, then recovered ~55 s later; the failing publishes therefore align with an injected checkout<->kafka network partition. Metrics confirm frontend-proxy ingress error spans at ~95-150 per 5 min from the first available sample (09:54:03Z) through 10:09 and rising to ~372 by 10:19, with checkout's error spans exclusively on "orders publish". Separately, the ad container was OOMKilled (exit 137, finishedAt 10:06:44Z) after growing to 468.9 MB against a 471.9 MB limit, and frontend GET /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds errors then rose 10:08-10:19; that is a second, later contribution to the proxy error rate and is reported as a hypothesis, not the onset cause. The conclusion is partial because the alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (the 1.6 value's expression is unverified), metric series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total begin only at 09:54:03Z (after the 09:49:03Z alert start), and chaos-mesh objects are not readable with the available tools, so the Schedule's activity at 09:49Z is inferred rather than observed.

claims.text: Chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh spawned a new NetworkChaos object every minute at :32 from 2026-11-17T10:08:32Z through 10:16:32Z ("Create new object: otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-<suffix>"); retained events begin only at 10:08:32Z.

Each spawned NetworkChaos reported "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l", "... otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-xclnk" and "... otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-skk8d", followed about 55 s later by "Successfully recover chaos" for the same three pods.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l logged, between 09:52:24Z and 09:52:59Z, repeated "Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open", "Failed to write message: kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker", and "client/metadata fetching metadata for [orders] from broker kafka:9092".

Trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 (start ~10:05:08Z) shows frontend-proxy ingress span with http.status_code=504 and otel.status_code=ERROR at 15.00 s, its "router frontend egress" span with error="true" and http.status_code="0", frontend POST /api/checkout at 89.08 s, checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder at 89.08 s, and checkout "orders publish" at 88.87 s with status ERROR and otel.status_description "circuit breaker is open".

frontend-proxy container logs record "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout with upstream host "frontend" and durations 15000-15014 ms at 09:55:22Z-09:55:57Z; the same 09:44-09:56Z window contains 261 matching 504 lines, so the 504s were already occurring around the 09:49:03Z alert start.

Increase of frontend-proxy error spans per 5 min was 142.2 on "ingress" at the first available sample (09:54:03Z), stayed between 95.3 and 150.0 through 10:09:03Z, then rose to 198.8, 252.2, 312.2, 358.9, 360.0 and 372.2 through 10:19:03Z; "router frontend egress" errors were 0 until the 10:08:03Z sample and then 15.6 -> 231.1 -> 8.9, mirroring the frontend failures.
checkout's error spans occur only on span_name "orders publish", at 130.0, 113.7, 123.3, 114.1, 146.7 and 138.9 per 5 min at the six 5-minute samples from 09:54:03Z to 10:19:03Z.

Pod ad-554b849958-4chjq container "ad" has lastState terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T10:06:44Z, restartCount 1, and is now running from 10:06:44Z with ready=true.

The ad container's memory working set rose from 425,181,184 bytes at 09:49:03Z to 468,869,120 bytes by 10:06:03Z and a second container instance (name 83ce518bc519...) appears from 10:07Z starting at 47,878,144 bytes; the ad container's memory limit is 471,859,200 bytes (450Mi), so the OOMKill occurred at the limit.

frontend error spans on "GET /api/data" and on "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" have identical series starting from 0 and rising to 14.4 at 10:08:03Z, peaking at 230.0 at 10:12:03Z, then falling to 10.0 at 10:19:03Z; frontend "tcp.connect" errors appear over the same interval (7.8-12.2 per 5 min).

At 10:19:00Z the 10-minute increase of error spans by service was frontend 1018.9, frontend-proxy 847.4, checkout 270.5, ad 39.0, fraud-detection 1.05, and 0 for accounting, payment and recommendation; cart, currency, email, product-catalog, quote and shipping did not appear in that error-series result.

At query time the pods checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l, kafka-ff7884766-xclnk, kafka-ff7884766-skk8d, frontend-675fd7b5c5-djtdf and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-59tsm are all Running/ready with restartCount 0, with container start times at 09:37-09:38Z.

The frontend-proxy pod itself is not failing: its container has restartCount 0 and has run since 09:37:08Z, and its access log records 200 responses for "GET /api/cart", "GET /api/products/..." and "POST /api/cart" in the same interval in which POST /api/checkout times out, so the 504s are upstream timeouts rather than a proxy crash.

Both Kafka pods (kafka-ff7884766-xclnk, kafka-ff7884766-skk8d) are Running and ready with restartCount 0, so a crashed broker process is not what the checkout publish failures show; they show loss of connectivity/partition metadata while the brokers stay up.

The ad OOMKill is not the cause of the alert's onset: the OOMKill finished at 10:06:44Z, about 17 minutes after the alert started at 09:49:03Z, and frontend-proxy was already logging POST /api/checkout 504 upstream timeouts throughout 09:44-09:56Z.

The checkout<->kafka partition produced by Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition was already active at the 09:49:03Z alert start; this is inferred because the same failure signature (checkout publish failures with broker connectivity errors, proxy 504s on /api/checkout) is observed at 09:44-09:56Z while the retained chaos events only begin at 10:08:32Z and the metric series only begin at 09:54:03Z.

The ad OOMKill at 10:06:44Z contributed to the later rise in frontend-proxy error rate (ingress errors 198.8 -> 372.2 per 5 min, egress errors appearing from the 10:08:03Z sample) by making the ad service unavailable, which matches the identical frontend "GET /api/data" and "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" error series in 10:08-10:19Z; no ad-side error span or ad log line was observed, and the previous ad container's logs are unavailable, so the mechanism is not directly confirmed.

Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh) and confirm whether the recurring checkout<->kafka partition is intended test traffic; if not, pause/remove it and re-check the frontend-proxy error rate.

Verify the "orders" topic's partition metadata/leadership against kafka:9092 from the checkout network namespace to distinguish an injected partition from broker-side topic loss, since checkout logged "Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker" while both kafka pods stayed ready.

Review the ad deployment's memory limit (471,859,200 bytes) against its steady growth to that limit and treat the 10:06:44Z OOMKill as a separate reliability issue to fix or to rule in as a contributor.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules at all (no_data), so the rule's expression, threshold and the meaning of the reported current value 1.5999999999999999 cannot be verified; http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, though listed as available, returned no series and no metric name in this window.
Series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total begin at 2026-11-17T09:54:03Z, five minutes after the 09:49:03Z alert start, so no metric value exists for the alert onset instant.

Chaos-mesh NetworkChaos and Schedule objects cannot be read with the available tools (kind not supported), so the partition's spec (action, direction, target, duration) is unverified; only event text naming Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition and NetworkChaos otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-* is available.
Kubernetes events are retained only from 2026-11-17T10:08:32Z, so chaos activity before that time (including at the 09:49:03Z alert start) could not be observed.

The previous (OOM-killed) ad container's logs are unavailable ("previous terminated container not found"), so the ad-side symptom of the OOM is unknown and the OOM cause cannot be read from application logs.
Jaeger only returned traces for roughly 10:05-10:06Z (and reported no traces for other sampled windows), so there is no trace sample of the alert onset or of the ad-related /api/data failures.
cart, currency, email, product-catalog, quote and shipping returned no error-span series in the error-by-service query, which is an absence of matching series rather than verified zero errors.
next_steps: Locate the RequestErrorRate rule in the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that actually evaluated it and record its PromQL expression, so the reported 1.6 value can be tied to a specific span or request denominator.

Read the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition spec (and one spawned NetworkChaos) with cluster-admin tooling to confirm action=partition, direction and target selection, and correlate its history with the 09:49:03Z alert start.
Cross-check kafka broker and topic health for the "orders" topic around 09:44-10:20Z using kafka-side metrics or broker logs, to independently confirm the partition hypothesis.
If ad instability is in scope, capture ad heap/memory profiles and restart history to decide whether the 450Mi limit is too low or the service leaks.
